expectedText:
CIVIL AIR PATROL LEAVE — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme, Inc.

ABOUT THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes the Civil Air Patrol Employment Protection Act, Labor Code §§ 1500-1507, which gives an eligible employee at a covered California employer the right to unpaid leave to respond to an emergency operational mission of the California Wing of the Civil Air Patrol, protects the employee's Civil Air Patrol membership and service from discrimination or discharge, and requires reinstatement to an equivalent position afterward. It does not cover the corpus's separate volunteer firefighter, reserve peace officer, and emergency rescue personnel leave document (Labor Code §§ 230.3-230.4), which is a different statute with different definitions, a different employer-size threshold, and a different enforcement route; it also does not cover jury duty, witness leave, or USERRA military leave, addressed elsewhere in this corpus.

WHO AND WHAT IS COVERED: KEY DEFINITIONS
Labor Code § 1501 defines four terms used throughout this part. "Civil Air Patrol leave" means leave requested by an employee who is a volunteer member of the California Wing of the Civil Air Patrol (the civilian auxiliary of the United States Air Force) and who has been duly directed and authorized by the U.S. Air Force, the California Emergency Management Agency, or another political subdivision of the state with authority to authorize an emergency operational mission, to respond to that mission within or outside California. "Employee" means a person permitted, required, or directed by an employer for wages or pay to engage in any employment, who has been employed by that employer for at least a 90-day period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave. "Employee benefits" means all benefits other than salary and wages, including group life insurance, health insurance, disability insurance, and pensions. "Employer" means any person, partnership, corporation, association, or other business entity, or the State of California, a municipality, or other unit of local government, that employs more than 15 employees.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(a) “Civil Air Patrol leave” means leave requested by an employee who is a volunteer member of the California Wing of the civilian auxiliary of the United States Air Force commonly known as the Civil Air Patrol and who has been duly directed and authorized by the United States Air Force, the California Emergency Management Agency, or other political subdivision of the State of California that has the authority to authorize an emergency operational mission of the California Wing of the Civil Air Patrol, to respond to an emergency operational mission, within or outside of the state, of the California Wing of the Civil Air Patrol.(b) “Employee” means a person who may be permitted, required, or directed by an employer for wages or pay to engage in any employment and who has been employed by that employer for at least a 90-day period immediately preceding the commencement of leave, if otherwise eligible for leave.(c) “Employee benefits” means all benefits, other than salary and wages, provided or made available to an employee by an employer and includes group life insurance, health insurance, disability insurance, and pensions, regardless of whether benefits are provided by a policy or practice of an employer.(d) “Employer” means any person, partnership, corporation, association, or other business entity; or the State of California, a municipality, or other unit of local government; that employs more than 15 employees."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 1501 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Lab. Code § 1501(a)-(d), definitions of Civil Air Patrol leave, employee, employee benefits, and employer (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1501.)
  Known gap: The § 1501(d) "employer" definition (more than 15 employees) is defined only "in this part" (Labor Code Part 5) and this document does not assert it matches the employee-count threshold used by any other California leave or anti-discrimination statute (for example, FEHA's 5-employee threshold or the 50-employee threshold in this corpus's separate volunteer-responder training-leave document); each statute sets its own threshold independently. The statute does not define how "more than 15 employees" is counted (full-time versus part-time, a rolling headcount, or employees at affiliated entities), and this document does not resolve that gap. The § 1501(b) "employee" definition ends with the circular phrase "if otherwise eligible for leave," and the verified text does not itself state what makes an employee "otherwise eligible" beyond the 90-day tenure requirement and the leave conditions described in the other clauses of this document.

RIGHT TO UP TO 10 DAYS OF UNPAID LEAVE PER CALENDAR YEAR
Under Labor Code § 1503(a)(1), a covered employer must provide not less than 10 days per calendar year of unpaid Civil Air Patrol leave to an employee responding to an emergency operational mission of the California Wing of the Civil Air Patrol. Leave for a single mission cannot exceed three days unless an extension is both granted by the governmental entity that authorized the mission and separately approved by the employer. Under § 1503(a)(2), an employer is not required to grant this leave to an employee who is required to respond to the same or another simultaneous emergency operational mission as a first responder or disaster service worker for a local, state, or federal agency.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(a) (1) An employer shall provide not less than 10 days per calendar year of unpaid Civil Air Patrol leave to an employee responding to an emergency operational mission of the California Wing of the Civil Air Patrol. Civil Air Patrol leave for a single emergency operational mission shall not exceed three days, unless an extension of time is granted by the governmental entity that authorized the emergency operational mission, and the extension of the leave is approved by the employer.(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), an employer is not required to
					 grant Civil Air Patrol leave to an employee who is required to respond to either the same or other simultaneous emergency operational mission as a first responder or disaster service worker for a local, state, or federal agency."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 1503 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Lab. Code § 1503(a)(1)-(2), 10-day annual entitlement, 3-day per-mission cap, and first-responder exception (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1503.)
  Known gap: The three-day per-mission cap can only be extended if two separate approvals both occur — the authorizing governmental entity's extension of time, and the employer's own approval of that extended leave — and the statute does not state what happens if one is given without the other. The § 1503(a)(2) exception turns on whether the employee is "required to respond" to a simultaneous mission "as a first responder or disaster service worker," and the verified text does not itself define either of those two terms for purposes of this part, so this document does not state which job titles or roles qualify beyond the statute's own bare language. The raw HTML for § 1503(a)(2) contains a mid-sentence line wrap (a tab-and-newline sequence between "required to" and "grant") that both independently fetched copies of the page reproduced identically; the quoted text below preserves it exactly rather than silently normalizing it.

NOTICE AND CERTIFICATION REQUIREMENTS
Under Labor Code § 1503(b)(1), an employee must give the employer as much notice as possible of the intended dates the Civil Air Patrol leave will begin and end. Under § 1503(b)(2), the employer may require certification from the proper Civil Air Patrol authority to verify the employee's eligibility for the leave, and the employer may deny the leave if the employee fails to provide that required certification.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(b) (1) An employee shall give the employer as much notice as possible of the intended dates upon which the Civil Air Patrol leave will begin and end.(2) An employer may require certification from the proper Civil Air Patrol authority to verify the eligibility of the employee for the leave requested or taken. The employer may deny the
					 leave to be taken as Civil Air Patrol leave if the employee fails to provide the required certification."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 1503 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Lab. Code § 1503(b)(1)-(2), notice and certification requirements (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1503.)
  Known gap: The statute's notice standard ("as much notice as possible") is not tied to any specific number of days or a written-notice requirement, and this document does not state a numeric deadline because the verified text does not set one. The statute does not specify what form Civil Air Patrol certification must take, which official may issue it, or how quickly the employee must produce it after a request, so this document does not describe a certification procedure beyond what § 1503(b)(2) itself says. As with the leave-entitlement clause, the raw HTML for § 1503(b)(2) contains a mid-sentence line wrap (between "deny the" and "leave") that both independently fetched copies reproduced identically; it is preserved exactly in the quoted text below.

LEAVE IS UNPAID UNLESS THE EMPLOYER CHOOSES OTHERWISE, AND OTHER LEAVE CANNOT BE FORCED FIRST
Labor Code § 1503(a)(1) itself describes the entitlement as "unpaid Civil Air Patrol leave." Under § 1503(c), an employee taking leave under this part is not required to exhaust all accrued vacation leave, personal leave, compensatory leave, sick leave, disability leave, or any other available leave in order to take Civil Air Patrol leave. Under § 1503(d), nothing in the statute prevents an employer from choosing to provide paid leave instead.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(c) An employee taking leave under this part shall not be required to exhaust all accrued vacation leave, personal leave, compensatory leave, sick leave, disability leave, and any other leave that may be available to the employee in order to take Civil Air Patrol leave.(d) Nothing in this act prevents an employer from providing paid leave for leave taken pursuant to this part."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 1503 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Lab. Code § 1503(c)-(d), no forced exhaustion of other leave, and employer option to pay (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1503.)
  Known gap: Section 1503(d) permits, but does not require, an employer to pay for this leave, and the statute does not itself create any wage-replacement benefit, state disability insurance eligibility, or other income-replacement mechanism for the unpaid days; this document does not address whether or how an employee might separately qualify for a different wage-replacement program during a period of Civil Air Patrol leave, because § 1503 is silent on that question. The no-forced-exhaustion rule in § 1503(c) protects the employee from being compelled to draw down other leave balances, but it does not itself say whether an employee may voluntarily elect to use paid leave concurrently, only that the employer cannot require it.

PROTECTION AGAINST DISCRIMINATION BASED ON CIVIL AIR PATROL MEMBERSHIP
Under Labor Code § 1502, an employer shall not discriminate against or discharge from employment a member of the Civil Air Patrol because of that membership, and shall not hinder or prevent a member from performing service as part of the California Wing of the Civil Air Patrol during an emergency operational mission for which the member is entitled to leave under this part.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "An employer shall not discriminate against or discharge from employment a member of the Civil Air Patrol because of such membership and shall not hinder or prevent a member from performing service as part of the California Wing of the Civil Air Patrol during an emergency operational mission of the California Wing of the Civil Air Patrol for which a member is entitled to leave under this part."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 1502 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Lab. Code § 1502, prohibition on discrimination based on Civil Air Patrol membership (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1502.)
  Known gap: Section 1502 states the prohibition itself but does not, in its own text, specify a remedy for its violation; the remedies and enforcement mechanism this document describes elsewhere (reinstatement rights under § 1504, the anti-retaliation provision of § 1506, and the civil action authorized by § 1507) are stated in separate sections of this same part, not within § 1502 itself, so this clause does not restate them here. The protection against being hindered from "performing service" is not, by its own terms, expressly limited to the specific 10-day/3-day leave allowance described in § 1503; this document does not resolve whether § 1502's protection against hindering service extends beyond days that would otherwise qualify as Civil Air Patrol leave under § 1503, because the verified text does not itself draw that boundary.

RIGHT TO REINSTATEMENT AFTER LEAVE
Under Labor Code § 1504(a), upon expiration of a leave authorized by this part, an employer must restore the employee to the position held when the leave began, or to a position with equivalent seniority status, employee benefits, pay, and other terms and conditions of employment. An employer may decline to restore an employee as required by this subdivision because of conditions unrelated to the employee's exercise of rights under this part. Under § 1504(b), the employer and employee may negotiate for the employer to maintain the employee's benefits, at the employer's expense, during the leave.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(a) An employer shall, upon expiration of a leave authorized by this part, restore an employee to the position held by him or her when the leave began or to a position with equivalent seniority status, employee benefits, pay, and other terms and conditions of employment. An employer may decline to restore an employee as required in this subdivision because of conditions unrelated to the exercise of rights under this part by the employee.(b) An employer and an employee may negotiate for the employer to maintain the benefits of the employee at the expense of the employer during the leave."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 1504 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Lab. Code § 1504(a)-(b), reinstatement duty and benefits-continuation negotiation (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1504.)
  Known gap: Section 1504(a)'s exception for declining restoration “because of conditions unrelated to the exercise of rights under this part” is not defined or illustrated by any list of qualifying conditions in the verified text (for example, it does not name layoffs, reorganization, or position elimination as examples), so this document does not state which employer circumstances would qualify, only that the statute allows some unspecified category of unrelated conditions to excuse restoration. Section 1504(b) is a negotiation mechanism, not a mandate: nothing in the verified text requires an employer to agree to maintain paid benefits during the leave, only that the parties may negotiate for it.

NO LOSS OF PREVIOUSLY ACCRUED BENEFITS, AND EFFECT ON COLLECTIVE BARGAINING AGREEMENTS
Under Labor Code § 1505(a), taking Civil Air Patrol leave does not result in the loss of an employee benefit accrued before the leave began. Under § 1505(b), this part does not affect an employer's obligation to comply with any collective bargaining agreement or employee benefit plan that provides greater leave rights than this part provides. Under § 1505(c), the rights provided by this part cannot be diminished by a collective bargaining agreement or employee benefit plan entered into on or after January 1, 2010. Under § 1505(d), this part does not affect or diminish the contract rights or seniority status of an employee who is not entitled to Civil Air Patrol leave.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(a) Taking Civil Air Patrol leave under this part shall not result in the loss of an employee benefit accrued before the date on which the leave began.(b) This part does not affect the obligation of an employer to comply with any collective bargaining agreement or employee benefit plan that provides greater leave rights to employees than the rights provided under this part.(c) The rights provided under this part shall not be diminished by any collective bargaining agreement or employee benefit plan entered into on or after January 1, 2010.(d) This part does not affect or diminish the contract rights or seniority
					 status of an employee not entitled to Civil Air Patrol leave."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 1505 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Lab. Code § 1505(a)-(d), no loss of accrued benefits and effect on collective bargaining agreements (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1505.)
  Known gap: Section 1505(c)'s anti-diminishment protection is expressly limited to collective bargaining agreements or benefit plans entered into “on or after January 1, 2010”; the verified text does not state what effect, if any, this part has on an agreement or plan that predates that date, and this document does not resolve that gap. The raw HTML for § 1505(d) contains a mid-sentence line wrap (a tab-and-newline sequence between "seniority" and "status") that both independently fetched copies reproduced identically; it is preserved exactly in the quoted text below rather than silently normalized.

PROHIBITION ON INTERFERENCE AND RETALIATION
Under Labor Code § 1506(a), an employer shall not interfere with, restrain, or deny the exercise or attempted exercise of a right established by this part. Under § 1506(b), an employer shall not discharge, fine, suspend, expel, discipline, or otherwise discriminate against an employee who exercises a right provided under this part or who opposes a practice made unlawful by this part.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(a) An employer shall not interfere with, restrain, or deny the exercise or the attempt to exercise a right established by this part.(b) An employer shall not discharge, fine, suspend, expel, discipline, or in any other manner discriminate against an employee who does any of the following:(1) Exercises a right provided under this part.(2) Opposes a practice made unlawful by this part."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 1506 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Lab. Code § 1506(a)-(b), prohibition on interference and retaliation (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1506.)
  Known gap: Section 1506 states the prohibition on interference and retaliation but, unlike Labor Code § 230.4 in this corpus's separate volunteer-responder document (which expressly cross-references a Labor Commissioner complaint procedure under § 98.7 with a one-year filing deadline), this part contains no cross-reference to § 98.7 or any other administrative complaint procedure, and no statute-specific limitations period for a private civil action is stated anywhere in §§ 1500-1507. This document does not assert what limitations period applies to a § 1506 claim, because the verified text of this part does not state one.

ENFORCEMENT: A PRIVATE CIVIL ACTION, NOT AN ADMINISTRATIVE COMPLAINT
Under Labor Code § 1507(a), an employee may bring a civil action in the superior court of the appropriate county to enforce this part. Under § 1507(b), the court may enjoin any act or practice that violates this part and may order any equitable relief necessary and appropriate to redress the violation or to enforce this part.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(a) An employee may bring a civil action in the superior court of the appropriate county to enforce this part.(b) The court may enjoin any act or practice that violates this part and may order any equitable relief necessary and appropriate to redress the violation or to enforce this part."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 1507 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Lab. Code § 1507(a)-(b), private civil action and available equitable relief (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1507.)
  Known gap: Section 1507 is the only enforcement mechanism stated anywhere in Labor Code §§ 1500-1507: this part contains no administrative Labor Commissioner or Division of Labor Standards Enforcement complaint procedure (in contrast to the § 98.7 complaint route this corpus's separate volunteer-responder training-leave document describes for a Labor Code § 230.4 violation), and no misdemeanor or other criminal penalty for an employer's noncompliance (in contrast to the misdemeanor penalty Labor Code § 230.3(b) attaches to a willful refusal to reinstate). The verified text of § 1507(b) authorizes only an injunction and “equitable relief”; it does not itself mention compensatory damages, statutory penalties, or attorney's fees, and this document does not assert that any of those remedies are available under this part, because § 1507's own text does not name them. A CourtListener case-law search for judicial decisions construing this part (queries for "Civil Air Patrol Employment Protection Act" and for "Civil Air Patrol" together with Labor Code §§ 1500-1507) returned zero results rather than a rate-limit error, so this document proceeds on the statutory text alone and does not describe how any court has applied § 1507 in practice.

CIVIL AIR PATROL LEAVE REQUEST AND NOTICE
Jordan Lee requests Civil Air Patrol leave from Acme, Inc. under Labor Code §§ 1500-1507, in connection with an emergency operational mission of California Wing, Civil Air Patrol — Sacramento Squadron.

Employee's hire date (start of employment with Acme, Inc.): March 3, 2024
Approximate total employee count at Acme, Inc.: 40
Dates of Civil Air Patrol leave requested: September 8, 2026 through September 9, 2026
Days of Civil Air Patrol leave already used this calendar year (if any): _______________
Brief description of the emergency operational mission: _______________________________________________
Certification from the proper Civil Air Patrol authority attached? ☐ Yes ☐ No (if requested by Acme, Inc.)
Date this request is given to Acme, Inc.: _______________

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
Please sign below to acknowledge receipt of this information sheet and the leave request above.

Employee: Jordan Lee
Date: September 1, 2026

Received on behalf of Acme, Inc. by: _______________________________________________
Date: _______________
City/State: Oakland, California

expectedJSON.gap: Section 1504(a)'s exception for declining restoration “because of conditions unrelated to the exercise of rights under this part” is not defined or illustrated by any list of qualifying conditions in the verified text (for example, it does not name layoffs, reorganization, or position elimination as examples), so this document does not state which employer circumstances would qualify, only that the statute allows some unspecified category of unrelated conditions to excuse restoration. Section 1504(b) is a negotiation mechanism, not a mandate: nothing in the verified text requires an employer to agree to maintain paid benefits during the leave, only that the parties may negotiate for it.

expectedJSON.body: Under Labor Code § 1505(a), taking Civil Air Patrol leave does not result in the loss of an employee benefit accrued before the leave began. Under § 1505(b), this part does not affect an employer's obligation to comply with any collective bargaining agreement or employee benefit plan that provides greater leave rights than this part provides. Under § 1505(c), the rights provided by this part cannot be diminished by a collective bargaining agreement or employee benefit plan entered into on or after January 1, 2010. Under § 1505(d), this part does not affect or diminish the contract rights or seniority status of an employee who is not entitled to Civil Air Patrol leave.

expectedJSON.body: Under Labor Code § 1506(a), an employer shall not interfere with, restrain, or deny the exercise or attempted exercise of a right established by this part. Under § 1506(b), an employer shall not discharge, fine, suspend, expel, discipline, or otherwise discriminate against an employee who exercises a right provided under this part or who opposes a practice made unlawful by this part.

citations.quote: (a) An employer shall not interfere with, restrain, or deny the exercise or the attempt to exercise a right established by this part.(b) An employer shall not discharge, fine, suspend, expel, discipline, or in any other manner discriminate against an employee who does any of the following:(1) Exercises a right provided under this part.(2) Opposes a practice made unlawful by this part.

This document does not assert what limitations period applies to a § 1506 claim, because the verified text of this part does not state one.

expectedJSON.body: Under Labor Code § 1507(a), an employee may bring a civil action in the superior court of the appropriate county to enforce this part. Under § 1507(b), the court may enjoin any act or practice that violates this part and may order any equitable relief necessary and appropriate to redress the violation or to enforce this part.
